grade.rationale: The component is generally well structured and uses Angular signals effectively, but its virtualized focus handling can lose or unexpectedly reclaim keyboard focus, and filtered-tree navigation does not preserve hierarchical semantics. Browser-global telemetry also weakens isolation and robustness.

summary: The implementation is clear and cohesive overall. The main risks are keyboard accessibility under virtualization, incorrect parent/child navigation while filtering, and tightly coupled diagnostic instrumentation. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied.

grade.rationale: Core selection, expansion, and virtualization logic is coherent, but focus can be stranded during recycling and hierarchical keyboard navigation becomes incorrect for filtered results.
Names, comments, and method boundaries are strong. Focus recovery and performance instrumentation nevertheless embed subtle lifecycle and platform assumptions.
The code is readable and unusually well documented, although the documented focus-ownership model does not fully explain or handle an active row leaving the rendered window.
Ordinary empty-state conditions are guarded, but nonessential performance instrumentation is not isolated from unavailable or failing browser APIs.
Most state transformations are separable, but direct dependencies on document, performance, requestAnimationFrame, console, and timers require extensive browser-global setup in unit tests.

findings.title: Virtualization can remove the focused row without providing a replacement
findings.description: The rendered window is derived solely from scroll position, while focus restoration searches that window only for the existing activeId. If a user scrolls the focused row beyond the overscan region, Angular removes its DOM element and the restoration target is absent. The focus-out handler deliberately preserves treeHasFocus when relatedTarget is null, so focus can remain stranded outside the tree; later scrolling or rendering can also unexpectedly return focus to the old row.
findings.recommendation: Keep the active row rendered while it owns DOM focus, or re-anchor activeId to an appropriate visible row before recycling it. Distinguish DOM recycling from genuine null-relatedTarget focus departures, such as window deactivation or programmatic blur, so later renders do not steal focus.

findings.title: Arrow navigation treats unrelated filtered matches as parents or children
findings.description: Filtering flattens the entire expanded tree and then removes nonmatching rows. In that result set, the row after an expanded directory is not necessarily its child, yet ArrowRight selects it. ArrowLeft similarly chooses the nearest earlier row with a smaller depth, which may be an unrelated match rather than the node's ancestor. This makes keyboard navigation dependent on incidental result order and violates tree-navigation expectations.
findings.recommendation: Retain explicit parent relationships in filtered results and navigate only to a visible child or actual ancestor. Alternatively, present search results with list-style keyboard behavior and disable expansion-oriented Left/Right semantics while a query is active.

findings.title: Toggle behavior is coupled to unguarded browser-global telemetry
findings.description: Every expansion schedules a global requestAnimationFrame callback that directly invokes performance.measure and console.info. Tests and nonstandard rendering environments must provide all of these globals, and a failure in optional measurement code becomes an uncaught asynchronous error. Repeated measures are also retained unless another part of the application clears them.
findings.recommendation: Move telemetry behind an injectable service or small no-throw adapter with injectable clock and scheduler dependencies. Define a bounded policy for retained performance entries and clean up scheduled work when the component is destroyed.
